links.outcome: Agreement of ChatGPT cognitive test scoring with physician scoring
links.effect: GPT-3.5 differed from physicians on memory (P<0.001; 8 of 21 items) and language (P=0.009 healthy; P=0.002 stroke); GPT-4 showed no significant difference from physicians on memory (P=0.8).
links.quote: Among healthy subjects, there were significant differences in memory scores between the physician group, GPT-3.5 group, and GPT-4 group ( P < 0.001), with a significant difference in GPT-3.5 and physician group scores ( P < 0.001).

links.outcome: GPT-3.5 scoring discrepancies after refined prompts and scoring rules
links.effect: Refined interaction protocols and scoring rules reduced most GPT-3.5 vs physician differences; only memory sections 8 and 14 remained different (P<0.05).
links.quote: After testing, optimizing the interaction process and scoring rules can reduce most of the differences, with only differences observed in 8th and 14th sections of memory ( P < 0.05), and no significant differences observed in the rest ( P > 0.05) ( Figure 6 ).

unlisted_practices: Using LLMs to score standardized neuropsychological test responses as a supplement to clinician scoring

links.outcome: Agreement between AI-generated cognitive assessment scores and physician reference scores
links.effect: GPT-3.5 differed from physicians on healthy-participant memory (P < 0.001) and language (P = 0.009), and stroke-participant language (P = 0.002).
links.quote: Among healthy subjects, there were significant differences in memory scores between the physician group, GPT-3.5 group, and GPT-4 group ( P < 0.001), with a significant difference in GPT-3.5 and physician group scores ( P < 0.001).

unlisted_practices: Refining task-specific scoring instructions and interaction protocols to improve GPT-3.5 agreement with physician assessments; after refinement, significant differences remained only in the 8th and 14th memory sections (P < 0.05).

links.effect: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 scores differed significantly (p<0.001), and GPT-4 showed no significant difference from physician scores (p=0.8).
links.quote: There was a significant difference in GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 group scores ( P < 0.001), while there was no significant difference in GPT-4 and physician group scores ( P = 0.8) ( Figure 1 ).

links.effect: GPT-3.5 had significant discrepancies in 8 out of 21 specific memory measures compared to physician assessments (p<0.05).
links.quote: Furthermore, within the domain of memory evaluation, GPT-3.5 exhibited discrepancies in 8 out of 21 specific measures when compared to assessments conducted by physicians (P < 0.05).

unlisted_practices: optimizing few-shot prompt interaction and scoring criteria instructions to reduce LLM assessment discrepancies against physicians
